orig_commit_message: Align byMethod and byContent, and introduce public API for using them outside of Context.
improved_commit_message: Refactor Naming: Change 'Block' to 'Handler' in Content Negotiation classes.
change_summary: The refactor involved renaming occurrences of 'Block' to 'Handler' in the ContentNegotiationHandler and ByContentSpec classes to improve clarity and maintainability. The changes also include renaming related parameter and attribute names in methods and classes while introducing new handler interfaces to facilitate better usage documentation and coding standards.
hints: Changed the 'Block' type to 'Handler' for improved clarity.
Updated multiple methods in ByContentSpec interface to use 'Handler' instead of 'Block'.
Renamed attributes from 'blocks' to 'handlers' in ContentNegotiationHandler and DefaultByContentSpec classes.
Updated method parameters and documentation to consistently reflect the 'Handler' type.

orig_commit_message: Rework mapIfOrElse and friends, introducing Function.when() and Function.conditional().
improved_commit_message: Refactor 'whenOrElse' and 'mapIfOrElse' methods to 'when' and 'mapIf' respectively for clarity and consistency.
change_summary: All instances of 'whenOrElse' have been renamed to 'when', paralleled by corresponding updates to parameters from 'ifAction' and 'elseAction' to 'onTrue' and 'onFalse'. Similarly, 'mapIfOrElse' methods were renamed to 'mapIf' with adjusted parameter names. This refactoring enhances readability and aligns method semantics across implementations.
hints: Renamed method 'mapIfOrElse' to 'mapIf' with parameters adjusted for clarity.
Renamed method 'whenOrElse' to 'when' with similar parameter renaming in all related methods.
Updated usage in examples and documentation comments to reflect the new method names.
Ensured all parameter names are consistently changed to 'onTrue' and 'onFalse' for better understanding of their roles.

+ * This is equivalent to {@link #when(Predicate, Function, Function) when(predicate, function, identity())}. + * + * @param predicate the condition for the argument + * @param function the function to apply if the predicate applies + * @param the type of argument and return value + * @return a function that delegates to the given function if the predicate applies, else returns the argument + * @see #when(Predicate, Function, Function) + * @see #conditional(Function, Action) + * @since 1.5 + */ + static Function when(Predicate predicate, Function function) { + return when(predicate, function, Function.identity()); + } + + /** + * Creates a function that delegates to the first function if the given predicate applies, else the second function. + * + * @param predicate the condition for the argument + * @param onTrue the function to apply if the predicate applies + * @param onFalse the function to apply if the predicate DOES NOT apply + * @param the type of argument + * @param the type of return value + * @return a function that delegates to the first function if the predicate applies, else the second argument + * @see #when(Predicate, Function) + * @see #conditional(Function, Action) + * @since 1.5 + */ + static Function when(Predicate predicate, Function onTrue, Function onFalse) { + return Exceptions.uncheck(() -> conditional(onFalse, s -> s.when(predicate, onTrue))); + } + + /** + * A spec for adding conditions to a conditional function. + * + * @param the input type + * @param the output type + * @see #conditional(Function, Action) + * @since 1.5 + */ + interface ConditionalSpec { + + /** + * Adds a conditional function. + * + * @param predicate the condition predicate + * @param function the function to apply if the predicate applies + * @return {@code this} + */ + ConditionalSpec when(Predicate predicate, Function function); + } + + /** + * Creates a function that delegates based on the specified conditions. + *

+ * If no conditions match, an {@link IllegalArgumentException} will be thrown. + * Use {@link #conditional(Function, Action)} alternatively to specify a different “else” strategy. + * + * @param conditions the conditions + * @param the input type + * @param the output type + * @return a conditional function + * @see #conditional(Function, Action) + * @throws Exception any thrown by {@code conditions} + * @since 1.5 + */ + static Function conditional(Action> conditions) throws Exception { + return conditional(i -> { + throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unhandled argument: " + i); + }, conditions); + } + + /** + * Creates a function that delegates based on the specified conditions. + *

+ * If no condition applies, the {@code onElse} function will be delegated to. + * + * @param onElse the function to delegate to if no condition matches + * @param conditions the conditions + * @param the input type + * @param the output type + * @return a conditional function + * @see #conditional(Action) + * @throws Exception any thrown by {@code conditions} + * @since 1.5 + */ + static Function conditional(Function onElse, Action> conditions) throws Exception { + ImmutableList.Builder> builder = ImmutableList.builder(); + conditions.execute(new ConditionalSpec() { + @Override + public ConditionalSpec when(Predicate predicate, Function function) { + builder.add(new ConditionalFunction.Branch(predicate, function)); + return this; + } + }); + + return new ConditionalFunction<>(builder.build(), onElse); + } }

+

+

change_summary: All instances of 'Overrides' have been replaced with 'Impositions' across the codebase. This includes renaming the package, methods, parameters, and attributes to better represent their functionality, improving overall code readability and understanding.
hints: Renamed the package from ratpack.override to ratpack.impose to better align with naming conventions.
Updated method names from 'getOverrides()' to 'getImpositions()' to reflect the new terminology.
Changed parameter and attribute names to 'impositions' throughout the affected classes to maintain consistency.
Refactored several methods that previously utilized Overrides to now utilize Impositions, ensuring that functionality remains intact while improving clarity.

change_summary: This refactoring involved renaming variable, method, and parameter names from 'sslClientAuth' to 'requireClientSslAuth' throughout the codebase to enhance clarity and better express the requirement for client SSL authentication. The changes were consistently applied to ensure cohesion across different classes and interfaces.

Updated method names to reflect new terminology: isSSLClientAuth became isRequireClientSslAuth.
Modified parameter names in ServerConfig.Builder and DefaultServerConfig to requireClientSslAuth.
Ensured attribute names in ServerConfigData were updated to match the new naming convention.

change_summary: This commit encapsulates a series of refactorings that primarily focus on renaming classes and method parameters for clearer semantics. The major change includes the renaming of the `HeaderHandler` class to `RouteHandler` to better reflect its functionality, followed by parameter renaming across multiple methods to standardize naming conventions and improve readability.
hints: Renamed `ratpack.http.internal.HeaderHandler` to `ratpack.http.internal.RouteHandler` to clarify its role in handling routing logic.
Updated the parameter name `context` to `ctx` in the method `handle(ctx Context)` to follow common abbreviation practices.
Changed parameter names such as `headerName` to `test` in the method signatures to emphasize the purpose of the parameters.
Streamlined method parameters by renaming `registryAction` to `action` in several methods to simplify and align with standard naming conventions.
Reorganized and removed multiple methods that were not being utilized effectively to declutter the codebase.

orig_commit_message:
Remove the Groovy overloads of byMethod and byContent to avoid ambiguous coercion issues when not using the Groovy DSL and using Groovy code.

Closes #692.
improved_commit_message: Refactor: Rename 'Handler' to 'Block' for clarity
change_summary: This commit renames multiple parameters, attributes, and variables from 'Handler' to 'Block' across the DefaultByContentSpec and DefaultByMethodSpec classes, as well as adjustments in related classes such as MultiMethodHandler and ContentNegotiationHandler. The intent is to improve the clarity of the code by ensuring consistent terminology that better reflects the functionality of the objects being used.
hints: Renamed Parameter 'handler' to 'block' in DefaultByContentSpec methods.
Updated Map attributes and parameters from Handler to Block type.
Consistently changed method signatures to replace Handler with Block.
Refactored methods in DefaultByMethodSpec to use Block instead of Handler.
Modified instances of MultiMethodHandler and ContentNegotiationHandler to follow the new Block naming convention.

orig_commit_message:
Move Pac4j to the new session API, and improvements to that API.

Also had to upgrade to latest Netty along the way.
improved_commit_message: Refactor parameter names and class renames for improved clarity and consistency
change_summary: This commit primarily involves renaming various parameters and classes across multiple files for consistency and clarity. Key changes include renaming parameters from 'context' to 'ctx', 'expiresDuration' to 'expires', and various class names to better reflect their purpose. These adjustments aim to enhance the understanding and maintainability of the codebase.
hints: Renamed method parameters for better readability and uniformity.
Updated class names to reflect their roles more effectively.
Utilized a consistent naming convention throughout the codebase.

+ * The session data can be obtained via the {@link Session#getData()} method. + *

+ * Every item is stored with a {@link SessionKey}. + * A key is comprised of a type (as a {@code Class}) and an optional name. + * The combination of type and name identifies the value. + * Two keys with differing types but identical names are not considered to be equivalent. + *

+ * When writing session data, the values are serialized immediately. + * That is, all objects are treated as immutable value objects from the perspective of this object. + * Any changes made to an object after it has been written to this object will NOT be persisted. + * If such changes are to be persisted, the object must be written again. + *

+ * The session data is held in memory for a given request until the {@link Session#save()} method is called on the corresponding session. + * However, this object internally holds the data in serialized form. + * Therefore, every read and write incurs the cost of serialization and deserialization. + */ +public interface SessionData { + + /** + * The keys of all objects currently in the session. + * + * @return the keys of all objects currently in the session + */ + Set> getKeys(); + + /** + * Fetch the object with the given key, using the {@link #getDefaultSerializer() default serializer}. + * + * @param key the key + * @param the type of object + * @return the value for the given key + * @see #require(SessionKey) + */ + default Optional get(SessionKey key) { + return get(key, getDefaultSerializer()); + } + + /** + * Read the object with the given key. + * + * @param key the key + * @param serializer the serializer + * @param the type of object + * @return the value for the given key + * @see #require(SessionKey, SessionSerializer) + */ + Optional get(SessionKey key, SessionSerializer serializer); + + /** + * Read the object with the given name, using the {@link #getDefaultSerializer() default serializer}. + *

+
+package ratpack.config.server
+
+import com.google.common.io.ByteSource
+import ratpack.config.ConfigData
+import ratpack.server.CompressionConfig
+import spock.lang.Specification
+
+import static com.google.common.base.Charsets.UTF_8
+
+@SuppressWarnings("GrMethodMayBeStatic")
+class CompressionConfigUsageSpec extends Specification {
+  def "can get CompressionConfig from no data"() {
+    given:
+    def configData = ConfigData.of().build()
+
+    when:
+    def config = configData.get(CompressionConfig)
+
+    then:
+    !config.compressResponses
+    config.minSize == CompressionConfig.DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_MIN_SIZE
+    config.mimeTypeWhiteList.empty
+    config.mimeTypeBlackList.empty
+  }
+
+  def "can override all CompressionConfig fields"() {
+    given:
+    def yamlData = """
+    |---
+    |compressResponses: true
+    |mimeTypeBlackList:
+    |  - image/png
+    |  - image/gif
+    |mimeTypeWhiteList:
+    |  - application/json
+    |  - text/plain
+    |minSize: 2048
+    """.stripMargin()
+    def configData = ConfigData.of().yaml(ByteSource.wrap(yamlData.getBytes(UTF_8))).build()
+
+    when:
+    def config = configData.get(CompressionConfig)
+
+    then:
+    config.compressResponses
+    config.minSize == 2048L
+    config.mimeTypeWhiteList == ["application/json", "text/plain"] as Set
+    config.mimeTypeBlackList == ["image/png", "image/gif"] as Set
+  }
+}

orig_commit_message: Replace LaunchConfig with ServerConfig and root Registry implementation.
improved_commit_message: Refactor LaunchConfig references to ServerConfig
change_summary: This refactor involves renaming all instances of 'LaunchConfig' to 'ServerConfig' across multiple classes and methods in the Ratpack codebase. +

orig_commit_message: Bust up DefaultExecController, and make the execution error and completion handlers immutable (i.e. specified at the start of the execution).
improved_commit_message: Refactor execution handling by renaming references to Execution and ExecutionBacking.
change_summary: This commit refactors the handling of execution within the Ratpack framework by renaming various components associated with Execution to ExecutionBacking. This includes parameters, attributes, variables, and methods. The motivation for this change is to provide better clarity and distinction between the execution constructs used in the framework, improving the overall understandability of the code base.
hints: Renamed parameters and attributes to reflect the new naming convention for ExecutionBacking.
All references to Execution have been updated to ExecutionBacking, including in methods and classes.
Utilized Factory pattern for creating ExecutionBacking instances instead of previously used Execution instances.
Updated method signatures and their implementations across multiple classes to maintain functionality while adhering to the new naming conventions.

* The execution object underpins an entire logical operation, even when that operation may be performed by multiple threads. *

- * The “execution” in Ratpack simulates aspects of the traditional execution context by allowing {@link #setErrorHandler(ratpack.func.Action) registration of an error handler} that is carried - * across execution segments (and therefore threads), and {@link #onComplete(Runnable) completion notifications}. - *

- * Importantly, it also serializes execution segments by way of the {@link #promise(ratpack.func.Action)} method. + * Importantly, it also serializes execution segments by way of the {@link ratpack.exec.ExecControl#promise(ratpack.func.Action)} method. * These methods are fundamentally asynchronous in that they facilitate performing operations where the result will arrive later without waiting for the result, * but are synchronous in the operations the perform are serialized and not executed concurrently or in parallel. * Crucially, this means that state that is local to an execution does not need to be thread safe.

orig_commit_message: Get rid of ExecContext and friends, replace with Execution.
improved_commit_message: Refactor exec context handling to execution.
change_summary: This commit renames several classes, methods, and parameters from 'Context' or 'ExecContext' to 'Execution' or related terms to improve clarity in the execution flow management. The `ExecContext` is now renamed to `Execution`, and related intricacies have been refactored to ensure that all dependencies appropriately reflect the new terminology.
hints: Renamed Classes: ExecContext to Execution, NoBoundContextException to ExecutionException, and RxRatpack.ContextBackedSubscriber to RxRatpack.ExecutionBackedSubscriber.
Renamed Methods: getContext to getExecution across various classes.
Updated method parameters to reflect new naming convention, focusing on improved semantic meaning.
Refactored variable names from context to execution to maintain consistency throughout the execution flow.
Implemented clear exception handling to use the new ExecutionException.

orig_commit_message:
Rename ModuleRegistry to BindingsSpec and make it not implement Registry.

Also renamed `modules {}` to `bindings {}` and some other methods.

Closes #323.
improved_commit_message: Refactor module-related classes and methods to use 'bindings' terminology instead of 'modules'.
change_summary: This commit renames various classes, methods, and attributes related to module handling in the Ratpack framework to use the more accurate term 'bindings'. The 'module' nomenclature is replaced to enhance clarity and alignment with encapsulation of binding behaviors. The goal is to improve the API for end-users by specifying bindings more clearly.
hints: Renamed 'GroovyModuleRegistry' to 'GroovyBindingsSpec' to reflect the change in functionality from module management to binding.
Updated methods such as 'modules()' to 'bindings()' throughout the codebase to ensure consistency.
Modified closures and action parameters to align with new 'BindingsSpec' terminology, making the refactoring extensive in affected classes.
Changed variable names from 'modulesConfigurer' and 'modulesAction' to 'bindingsConfigurer' and 'bindingsAction' to maintain semantic integrity.

Module order and overrides

+ *

+ * The order in which modules are added is significant. + * Subsequent modules can override the bindings of previous modules. + * This is a very useful technique for augmenting/customising the functionality provided by modules. + * Many modules provide extensive bindings to facilitate such overriding. + *

+ * This can be used to do post processing of registered objects or application initialisation. + * + * @param action the action to execute against the constructed injector + */ + void init(Action action); + + /** + * Registers a runnable to instantiated via dependency injection when the injector is created from this module registry. + *

+ * This facilitates writing a {@link Runnable} implementation that uses constructor injection to get hold of what it needs to for the initialization. + * + * @param clazz the class of the runnable to execute as an init action + */ + void init(Class clazz); + +}

orig_commit_message: Work on the unit testing bits.
improved_commit_message: Refactor handling classes and methods to align with updated terminology and structure.
change_summary: This commit includes a comprehensive refactoring of the handling classes within the ratpack testing framework. Key renames include 'Invocation' to 'HandlingResult', 'InvocationBuilder' to 'RequestFixture', and several associated classes and methods, improving clarity and consistency in naming conventions. Additionally, method signatures have been adjusted to enhance readability and maintainability.
hints: Renamed 'Invocation' to 'HandlingResult' to better reflect its purpose.
Transformed 'InvocationBuilder' into 'RequestFixture' to provide clearer context for request handling in tests.
Changed method 'invoke' in multiple classes to 'handle' for clearer action description.
Renamed timeout parameters for consistency in naming.
Consolidated test handling logic through new 'buildFixture' method.

+package ratpack.manual.snippets.executer
+
+import org.codehaus.groovy.control.MultipleCompilationErrorsException
+import org.codehaus.groovy.control.messages.SyntaxErrorMessage
+import ratpack.func.Transformer
+
+class ExceptionTransformer implements Transformer<Throwable, Throwable> {
+
+  final String sourceClassName
+  final String pre
+  final String sourceFileName
+  final int lineNumber
+
+  ExceptionTransformer(String sourceClassName, String pre, String sourceFileName, int lineNumber) {
+    this.sourceClassName = sourceClassName
+    this.pre = pre
+    this.sourceFileName = sourceFileName
+    this.lineNumber = lineNumber
+  }
+
+  @Override
+  Throwable transform(Throwable throwable) throws Exception {
+    def errorLine = 0
+
+    if (throwable instanceof CompileException) {
+        errorLine = throwable.lineNo
+    } else {
+      def frame = throwable.getStackTrace().find { it.fileName == sourceClassName }
+      if (frame) {
+        errorLine = frame.lineNumber
+      } else {
+        frame = throwable.getStackTrace().find { it.fileName == "Example.java" }
+        if (frame) {
+          errorLine = frame.lineNumber
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    errorLine = errorLine - pre.split("\n").size()
+    StackTraceElement[] stack = throwable.getStackTrace()
+    List<StackTraceElement> newStack = new ArrayList<StackTraceElement>(stack.length + 1)
+    newStack.add(new StackTraceElement(sourceClassName, "javadoc", sourceFileName, lineNumber + errorLine))
+    newStack.addAll(stack)
+    throwable.setStackTrace(newStack as StackTraceElement[])
+    throwable
+  }
+}

orig_commit_message:
Cleanup of methods that deal with adding to the context registry.

Closes #284.
improved_commit_message: Refactor and rename classes and methods for clarity
change_summary: This commit includes a series of refactorings that rename classes and methods to improve clarity and consistency across the codebase. Key renamings include 'RegisterForNextHandler' to 'RegistryNextHandler', 'RegisteringHandler' to 'RegistryInsertHandler', and updating several parameters and methods to use 'registry' instead of 'service'. This refactor aims to provide a clearer understanding of the roles of different handlers and their interactions with registry components.
hints: Renamed classes for clearer semantic meaning related to handling and registry actions.
Standardized parameter naming across methods to enhance code readability.
Replaced outdated and ambiguous names (e.g., 'service') with more relevant terms (e.g., 'registry').
Updated method signatures to improve clarity on the usage and expected types of parameters.

orig_commit_message:
More work decoupling the execution pieces.

Foreground/Background have been replaced with ExecController.
improved_commit_message: Refactor Ratpack Execution Model: Rename Foreground to ExecController and Background to Blocking, Update Method Interfaces
change_summary: The refactoring focuses on renaming the existing Foreground and Background concepts in the Ratpack execution model to more accurately represent their roles as ExecController and Blocking respectively. This change improves clarity and consistency across the codebase in relation to execution handling. All usages of the renamed types and methods were updated accordingly throughout the project.
hints: Renamed Foreground to ExecController to better reflect its responsibilities in managing execution context.
Renamed Background to Blocking, aligning with the new terminology representing blocking operations.
Reflected changes in method signatures across multiple classes including DefaultContext and LaunchConfig.
Updated import statements to remove references to the old Foreground and Background classes.
Ensured compatibility with existing functionality by appropriately forwarding calls to the new ExecController.

orig_commit_message:
More work decoupling the execution support (i.e. foreground/background) from request handling.

This opens the doors to executing pieces of work that aren't about request processing (i.e. scheduled jobs, test use of http client). The docs are in a bit of a mess after this and will be addressed in a subsequent commit.
improved_commit_message: Refactor and Rename Background and Context Handling Across Exec and File Modules
change_summary: This commit refactors the codebase by renaming several parameters, attributes, and classes related to background and context handling in Ratpack's execution and file modules. The goal was to improve code clarity by using more descriptive names that better reflect their purpose, such as changing 'background' to 'execContext' and 'contextStorage' to 'contextFactoryThreadLocal' where appropriate, thereby enhancing maintainability and readability.
hints: Renamed background parameters to execContext in various methods for better semantic clarity.
Changed contextStorage to contextFactoryThreadLocal to indicate its intended use for thread-local context suppliers.
Updated DefaultBackground and DefaultForeground classes to handle the new context naming conventions.
Revised method signatures across the file handling and execution contexts to reflect the renaming.
Modified interfaces and promise handling to align with the new context handling structure using ExecContext.

@@ -1,22 +0,0 @@
-# Backgrounding
-
-By default, Ratpack is based on [non blocking (or async) IO](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asynchronous_I/O) which is more efficient than blocking (or sync) IO based
-applications and therefore supports greater throughput.
-A key implication of this is that handlers must make special provisions if they do need to perform blocking IO.
-
-Non blocking apps use a small numbers of threads to handle requests, roughly equivalent to the number of processing units available to the JVM running the application.
-This is possible because these request threads are (ideally) always doing work instead of waiting for IO or doing long computations.
-This means that wherever possible you should use libraries to access external resources (e.g. files, databases, web services) that support asynchronous IO.
-However, this is not always possible.
-For example, many database access libraries only support blocking on IO.
-In such cases, you can use Ratpack's backgrounding support to perform the blocking operation off the request handling threads.
-
-Ratpack can also be used to write blocking applications (i.e. using a large thread pool for handling requests).
-This can result is simpler application code, but greatly reduced throughput.
-See [the “launching” chapter](launching.html) chapter for details on how to launch a Ratpack app in this mode.
-
-## The Background API
-
-The context object offers the [getBackground()](api/ratpack/exec/ExecContext.html#getBackground\(\)) method that returns a [Background](api/ratpack/exec/Background.html) object.
-This gives access to the background thread pool for performing blocking or long operations.
-The [background(Callable)](api/ratpack/exec/ExecContext.html#background\(java.util.concurrent.Callable\)) method provides a more convenient entry point for this API.
\ No newline at end of file

change_summary: This refactoring improves code readability and consistency by renaming various parameters and methods related to executor management. The term 'mainExecutor' has been replaced with 'foregroundExecutor' to clarify the purpose of these executors. Similarly, threading-related methods and parameters were renamed to use 'threads' instead of 'mainThreads', enhancing the clarity of their functionality across several classes, including DefaultBackground, LaunchConfig, and DefaultContext.
hints: Renamed 'mainExecutor' to 'foregroundExecutor' in DefaultBackground class to better represent its purpose.
Updated constructor in DefaultBackground to use 'foregroundExecutor' instead of 'mainExecutor'.
Refactored ApplicationConstants class to replace contextProvider with 'foreground' to reflect intended usage.
Standardized method and parameter names across the LaunchConfig and related classes from 'mainThreads' to 'threads'.
Removed outdated contextual provider methods to streamline the interface and improve clarity.
Ensured that all classes consistently utilize the 'Foreground' type instead of 'Provider<Context>' for better readability.

orig_commit_message: Rename “blocking” to “background”.
improved_commit_message: Refactor to replace 'Blocking' with 'Background' to clarify asynchronous operations
change_summary: This commit refactors the codebase by renaming references from 'Blocking' to 'Background' in various classes, methods, and parameters to better indicate the nature of the operations being performed. The changes enhance clarity about IO operations being offloaded without blocking request threads, emphasizing the use of background processes. Furthermore, several related names such as 'BlockingThreadFactory' were also updated to better reflect their new functionality.
hints: Renamed the class 'ratpack.launch.LaunchConfigBuilder.BlockingThreadFactory' to 'ratpack.launch.LaunchConfigBuilder.BackgroundThreadFactory'.
Changed the package names from 'ratpack.block' to 'ratpack.background'.
Updated method parameters and return types in the 'DefaultFileHttpTransmitter' and 'DefaultFileRenderer' classes.
Replaced references in the 'Context' interface to use 'Background' instead of 'Blocking'.
Changed variable names across multiple classes, particularly focused on executor services, to indicate background processing.
Updated Groovy context and other related files to adapt to new background processing methods.

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+# Backgrounding
+
+By default, Ratpack is based on [non blocking (or async) IO](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asynchronous_I/O) which is more efficient than blocking (or sync) IO based
+applications and therefore supports greater throughput.
+A key implication of this is that handlers must make special provisions if they do need to perform blocking IO.
+
+Non blocking apps use a small numbers of threads to handle requests, roughly equivalent to the number of processing units available to the JVM running the application.
+This is possible because these request threads are (ideally) always doing work instead of waiting for IO or doing long computations.
+This means that wherever possible you should use libraries to access external resources (e.g. files, databases, web services) that support asynchronous IO.
+However, this is not always possible.
+For example, many database access libraries only support blocking on IO.
+In such cases, you can use Ratpack's backgrounding support to perform the blocking operation off the request handling threads.
+
+Ratpack can also be used to write blocking applications (i.e. using a large thread pool for handling requests).
+This can result is simpler application code, but greatly reduced throughput.
+See [the “launching” chapter](launching.html) chapter for details on how to launch a Ratpack app in this mode.
+
+## The Background API
+
+The context object offers the [getBackground()](api/ratpack/handling/Context.html#getBackground\(\)) method that returns a [Background](api/ratpack/background/Background.html) object.
+This gives access to the background thread pool for performing blocking or long operations.
+The [background(Callable)](api/ratpack/handling/Context.html#background\(java.util.concurrent.Callable\)) method provides a more convenient entry point for this API.
+
+The Groovy API offers a more Groovy friendly API via the [background(Closure)](api/ratpack/groovy/handling/GroovyContext.html#background\(groovy.lang.Closure\)) of the
+[GroovyContext](api/ratpack/groovy/handling/GroovyContext.html) type.
\ No newline at end of file

orig_commit_message: Rename ServiceRegistry to Registry.
improved_commit_message: Refactor service registry references to a more generic registry structure.
change_summary: This commit consolidates various class and parameter names to use 'Registry' instead of 'ServiceRegistry', reflecting a shift towards a more streamlined and cohesive registry structure. The renaming also aids in improving code readability and maintains consistency across the codebase.
hints: Renamed 'ServiceRegistry' to 'Registry' in parameter lists and class definitions for consistency.
Updated method signatures and implementations to reflect the new naming conventions.
Replaced any references to related exceptions or classes, including 'NotInServiceRegistryException' to 'NotInRegistryException'.
Combined renaming changes in multiple classes that involved similar patterns to minimize errors.

+import com.google.common.collect.ImmutableList

+

+    when:

+    def object1 = new ObjectHoldingHierarchicalRegistry(root, 2)

+
+    then:
+    lazy.toString() == "LazyHierarchicalRegistry{${Integer.name}} -> ObjectServiceRegistry{3} -> ObjectServiceRegistry{2} -> RootRegistry{[1]}"
+  }
+}

orig_commit_message: Rename Context to ServiceRegistry.
improved_commit_message: Refactor context management to use services instead of contexts throughout the framework.
change_summary: This commit performs a substantial refactor of the Ratpack framework, replacing 'Context' with 'Service' terminology and updating relevant classes, methods, and attributes. The changes improve clarity and consistency across the system by aligning naming conventions with the concept of service management. Key refactorings include renaming classes like ContextInsertingHandler to ServiceInsertingHandler and updating the NettyHandlerAdapter to use RootServiceRegistry instead of RootContext.
hints: Renamed Context-related classes and interfaces to use Service terminology for better clarity.
Updated method signatures to replace context parameters with serviceRegistry parameters.
Refactored handlers to insert service contexts rather than contexts.
Revised relevant documentation comments to accurately reflect the change in terminology.
Ensured consistency in usage across the framework by renaming variables and attributes as needed.

orig_commit_message: Remove usage of the term "route" and "routing".
improved_commit_message: Refactor routing classes and methods to improve clarity and consistency.
change_summary: This commit performs a comprehensive renaming of classes, methods, and parameters related to routing in the Ratpack framework. The `RoutingHandler` class and its occurrences have been renamed to `ChainBuildingHandler` to better reflect its purpose. Additionally, methods such as `routes()` have been renamed to `chain()` and variables relating to routing were updated for consistency and clarity. This refactor aims to improve the understanding and maintainability of the codebase.
hints: Renamed `NettyRoutingAdapter` to `NettyHandlerAdapter` for clarity.
Renamed `RoutingHandler` to `ChainBuildingHandler` in multiple locations.
Changed method and variable names to use `chain` terminology instead of `routes`.
Updated method parameters from `routing` to `handlers` for better semantic meaning.
Consolidated all changes to maintain consistency across the codebase.

orig_commit_message:
Introduce RoutingBuilder instead of using Action<Routing>.

It's functionally the same thing, but gives us somewhere to document what a routing builder is all about… and makes the API more understandable… hopefully.

I'm not crazy about the name, but couldn't think of anything else.

change_summary: Renamed parameters, attributes, and variables from 'action' or 'routingAction' to 'builder' or 'routingBuilder' across various methods and classes, enhancing clarity regarding their purposes in the routing context.
hints: All instances of the 'action' parameter in routing methods have been replaced with 'builder' to more accurately represent the builder pattern being employed.
Action type references such as 'Action<? super Routing>' were replaced by 'RoutingBuilder' to provide better understanding of how routing is constructed.
Refactoring also adjusted related attributes in the RoutingHandler class to align with the new naming conventions.

improved_commit_message: Refactor package, classes, methods, parameters, and variables for improved clarity and consistency.
change_summary: This commit involves significant renaming of packages, classes, methods, parameters, and variables to enhance code readability and more accurately reflect their functionality. The package 'org.ratpackframework.assets' is renamed to 'org.ratpackframework.file' and various classes related to HTTP handling, routing, and asset requests have been revised for clearer naming conventions.
hints: Renamed CoreHttpHandlers to Handler for better abstraction in the new HTTP framework.

orig_commit_message: Bust out a separate Groovy module.
improved_commit_message: Refactor package and class names for clarity and consistency
change_summary: This commit involves a series of renamings to improve the clarity and consistency of the codebase. Key changes include renaming the package from 'org.ratpackframework.io' to 'org.ratpackframework.util', renaming classes to more accurately reflect their purpose, and updating method parameters and attributes to better communicate their role in the application. The motivation for these changes is to enhance maintainability and ease of understanding for developers working on the project.
hints: Renamed package for better alignment with utility functions.
Updated class names to more accurately describe their functionalities.
Adjusted method parameters to reflect new naming conventions.
Ensured that attribute names follow a consistent naming pattern for clarity.

The primary focus is on updating 'RoutedRequest' to 'Routed<HttpExchange>' to better reflect its purpose and usage context, alongside renaming various handler classes and related parameters accordingly.

Refactored 'NotFoundHandler', 'PathRouter', and 'ResponseFactory' to use the new 'Routed<HttpExchange>' type for better consistency in request handling.
Streamlined method signatures across the codebase to improve readability and maintainability.

orig_commit_message: Move from Vert.x to Netty.
improved_commit_message: Refactor class and method names for improved clarity and consistency
change_summary: This commit renames several classes, methods, and variables to better reflect their roles and functionalities in the codebase. Key changes include renaming of classes related to server and request-handling components, as well as more intuitive naming for variables and parameters within methods. This refactoring aims to enhance the readability and maintainability of the code.
hints: Renamed 'RatpackApp' to 'RatpackServer' to clarify its purpose as the server component.
Renamed 'HttpServerProvider' to 'InetSocketProvider' to better specify the socket functionality it provides.
Modified method signatures to replace generic names with more descriptive names.
Removed obsolete parameters and replaced them with more relevant versions to fit with RESTful patterns.
